sense: of a river or the sea

terms.grammar: noun, third declension; in this sense in set phrases
evidence: Caes. BG 7.58: secundō flūmine, with the current
Caes. BG 7.60: adversō flūmine, against the current
Traupman 203: current (in the sense of “the flow”), flūmen
terms.comment: Properly “a flowing” (Lewis & Short), and so the current itself: secundō flūmine, with the current, downstream; adversō flūmine, against it, upstream. The force of the current is vīs flūminis (Caes. BG 4.15; Traupman 203).

terms.gloss: a current at sea; the tide
evidence: Caes. BG 4.23: et ventum et aestum ūnō tempore … secundum
Caes. BG 4.17: propter lātitūdinem, rapiditātem altitūdinemque flūminis
terms.comment: Rare: Caesar’s word for the rush of the Rhine (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nōn aliter quam quī adversō vix flūmine lembum rēmigiīs subigit, sī bracchia forte remīsit, atque illum in praeceps prōnō rapit alveus amnī
phrases.english: just like a man who can barely row his boat against the current: if he happens to slacken his arms, the channel sweeps it headlong downstream

sources: Lewis & Short: flumen · Lewis & Short: secundus · Lewis & Short: adversus · Lewis & Short: aestus · Lewis & Short: rapiditas
